data.gender_notes: Leon is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word λέον (leon), meaning lion. In the Bible, the lion is a symbol of courage, power, and royalty. Leon may evoke feelings of bravery, nobility, and strength. In Christian tradition, the lion is also associated with the apostle St. Mark, who used the lion as a symbol in his gospel. The name Leon carries the meaning “Lion” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Leon usually hope their child will grow to embody lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Leon total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Leon has a rich cultural history and has been popular throughout Europe since ancient times. In the Middle Ages, it was a common name among royalty and nobility in France, Spain, and Portugal. Leon is also the name of multiple cities across Europe, including Leon in Spain and León in Guatemala and Nicaragua.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the image of the lion represents strength, courage, and the power of God. Saint Mark, one of the twelve apostles, uses the lion as a symbol in his gospel. This association makes the name Leon a powerful spiritual name for those who seek to embody courage, strength, and the power of God in their lives. The name also serves as a reminder of the lion of Judah, a symbol of Jesus, who is called "the lion of the tribe of Judah" in the book of Revelation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Leon derives from the Greek word "leon," meaning "lion." In Christianity, Leon is a symbol of courage, strength, and power, representing Christ's ability to conquer adversity. The name reminds us of Christ's strength in times of challenge.

historical_references.reference: The name Leon is derived from the Greek word 'leon', meaning 'lion'. In early Christian history, there were several saints named Leon. One of the most famous is Saint Leon the Philosopher, who lived in the 5th century AD. He was a pagan philosopher who converted to Christianity and became a bishop and a prominent theologian. His writings helped to clarify Christian doctrine and earn him the title 'The Lion of the Church'.

Another Saint Leon is Leon the African, who lived in the 11th century AD. He was a theologian and the founder of the first monastery in Algeria. Born in North Africa, he is also known as Leon of Carthage. His teachings helped to spread Christianity in Africa and earn him the title 'The Lion of Africa'.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Leon has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts. In the technology sector, there are several notable tech entrepreneurs and developers with this name, including Leonardo Cholodowski, the founder of the popular coding bootcamp Holberton School, and Leon Nakanishi, the co-founder of the mobile app development company Fueled. On social media platforms like Twitter and Instagram, 'Leon' is used as a casual, friendly term for anyone named Leon, often with humorous or endearing hashtags like #LeonLife or #LeonSquad. In the entertainment industry, Leonardo DiCaprio's continued success in film and activism keeps the name in the limelight. Overall, Leon is a name that signifies innovation, creativity, and a strong sense of community.
